children: Adobe Inc. (ADBE, Financials), the software giant behind Photoshop and Acrobat, is luring many customers to its AI products. Wall Street wants to know how much those users are worth.
JPMorgan analyst Arti Vula lowered her price objective on the stock to $315 from $340 after the company's fiscal third-quarter earnings but maintained her Buy rating.
Revenue climbed 12.8% to $6.76 billion from a year ago, exceeding estimates of $6.69 billion. Adjusted earnings of $6.13 per share also beat projections.
Even the AI numbers looked good. AI-first annual recurring income grew 150% to over $650 million and Creative freemium monthly active users topped 100 million, up 70%.

That's a massive funnel. But it hasn't yet become the kind of revenue investors want to see. Adobe is pushing back some of the planned price hikes for Creative Cloud as it focuses on engagement, and net new annual recurring income is still likely to fall this fiscal year.
That's why the stock dropped despite the company beating on results. JPMorgan still sees value, estimating Adobe trades at about eight times 2027 unlevered free cash flow.
The next test for investors is easy. Adobe has proven it can convince folks to use its AI technologies. Now it has to show that those users will pay enough to jump-start stronger growth.

title: JPMorgan Cuts Adobe Target to $315 as AI Monetization Concerns Persist
